title: Diagnose the 20.36 s Engram admission evaluate during TermAl's post-restart rebind burst
outcome: Diagnose the 20.36 s Engram admission evaluate during TermAl's post-restart rebind burst
acceptance: The time spent in the 20,359 ms admission evaluate for session-5135 at 2026-10-17 05:48:30Z is attributed by measurement to its phases: store open, SQLite lock or busy wait, query and projection work, and response serialization. If the evidence cannot settle the attribution, the record names the gap.

Under a reproduced or measured concurrent burst of named-root binds, claim renewals and admissions from about 10 sessions, the record shows whether admission latency grows with concurrency, and names the contended resource or rules out each candidate.

Either an in-scope Engram defect is filed or fixed with a test that reproduces the slow path, or the record concludes, with evidence, that the latency was outside Engram (host, disk or scheduling), with a cross-reference to the matching TermAl item.
disposal_reason: Obsolete on Greg's word (Asistant #239): the admission evaluate it would diagnose no longer exists. A general store-latency problem would be its own item with current evidence.
